task.title: Reconcile divergent task histories
task.description:
Replay local operations onto the fetched remote tip instead of leaving a divergent task ref. Integration behaves identically wherever a fetch already advances canonical refs, meaning fetch, sync, setup, and the auto-sync mutation path: fetch, then for each divergent task roll the canonical local ref back to the remote tip, park the orphaned commit under refs/workbook/reconciled/<task-id>/<n>, and replay each local-only operation pack onto the new parent as ordinary single-parent commits. A replayed pack keeps its actor, wall time, and operation ULIDs and rewrites only its logical clock. Most concurrent edits touch disjoint fields, commute, and replay silently, so a mutation that loses a push race and a fetch that finds week-old local work both republish without asking anything. Introduce no multi-parent commits; the single-parent tip and history rules in gitstore read and history validation stay unchanged.

Surface exactly three conflicts: both sides changed description; a replayed dependency set.add closes a cycle against the fetched graph; and an upstream tombstone leaves a local operation unable to apply. Each aborts replay for its own task and leaves that canonical ref at the fetched remote tip or the furthest advanced replayed local operation before the conflict arose. Report them through one conflict member in the result envelope carrying a list, because one fetch can conflict on several tasks at once, with each entry naming its task and a type discriminator. Description carries base, ours, and theirs; dependency carries the edge and the closing path; tombstone carries the blocked operation. Never write conflict markers or any unresolved value into a commit. Resolution is a plain retry of the ordinary command against the now fast-forwarded ref, so no reconcile command, no continue command, no discard flow, and no persistent conflict state exist anywhere. The contract is non-interactive and complete without a terminal so JSON output, hooks, agents, and the web board all use it; TTY prompting and web UI is a later affordance layered on top.

Reconcile per task rather than all or nothing. A divergent task should not stop blocking publication of unrelated tasks, so sync reconciles and publishes every task it can and reports the rest, matching the per-ref outcomes push already retains.

Make retryability answerable from the exit code alone. Add a conflict category with exit code 8, meaning read the envelope, change the input, then retry. Redefine 6 stale-write to mean the opposite: retry the identical command and it will probably succeed. Divergence and rejected pushes stop reporting 6 because they now reconcile, leaving 6 to cover local ref races and validation-cache races. Reclassify the equal-rank gap error in core service from stale-write to validation, since it is not a race and fails identically on every retry; replaying a move records its literal computed rank, so two clones can converge on equal ranks and reach it more often.

Treat every other concurrent field change as silent last-syncer-wins, including a replayed operation whose value already matches upstream, which records no commit. Prune parked refs for a task inside the existing update-ref transaction on the next successful mutation of that task from this clone, never on reads or fetches, keeping at most the last few per task. Parked refs stay local and are never pushed, which the taskRefPrefix-scoped ref enumerations already provide for free.

Rewrite the sync-divergent-tips benchmark topology to assert the new outcome, replacing its expectFailure and stale-write error-category contract with a reconciled and published result. Keep it measured with no target so it reports not-evaluated, and set a budget from observed evidence in later work rather than guessing one now. The cli-update scenario keeps its existing 200ms budget when no rejection occurs.

Out of scope: global dependency-cycle validation, since a cycle can already appear from two clean fast-forwards on different tasks with no conflict at all, and workbook next reporting no available task is the accepted signal; bounded replay retry, which hands back on the first rejection; selectively discarding local work before publishing, whose review surface belongs with the change history view in WB-01KZ1JCYZCPD156TCXMRB4Z6ZB; interactive prompting; three-way description merging, tracked in WB-01KZ24RAMB8QYSWZAYZXNZ25FX; and any change to serve beyond consuming the same contract.
